brief: The punt is bounded twice and the clock is not either bound. #128 measured 236 of 298 offers refused on TIME; #131 then built the last punt and the biggest refusal became BUSY at 85, because there is ONE hull doing a 5-7 h round trip. Separately, 28 of 87 deck offers land between 22h and 01h, which no round trip can return from. Answer the SUPPLY, not the window: a second hull, or a turnaround that does not cost the full trip. Fold in a two-line bug while you are in the file: `puntLampF()`'s lantern is drawn in the item pass and never registered, so `applyLight`'s multiply makes it slate and the last punt has carried an UNLIT light at night since #131 - `BARGE_LAMP` beside `BOAT_LAMP` is the pattern to copy. Why now: River is the longest-untouched domain after Roofs (last #131, 8 back), the premise is pre-counted by two earlier iterations, and an unlit lantern on a night crossing is a visible fault.
successLooksLike: Crossings per day up materially with BUSY no longer the top refusal, measured over 10 seeds x 26 days with the refusal reasons broken out CLAUSE BY CLAUSE in their own evaluation order (the existing punt probes show the idiom). The lantern reads as a flame at 22h in a night screenshot, not as slate. Census: `people` may churn; nothing structural should move.
avoid: Do not answer this by widening the window - #131 already priced the round trip against EVE_GONE and the late offers are arithmetically unreturnable. Do not give a second hull its own arrival source; the passengers already exist and are being refused. If you add a hull, two hulls nearer than ~0.9 cells render as one shape, and a moored pair needs PUNT_MOOR to hold two berths.
